title: HyperHarbor setup profile
description: What to install, remove, and change in a Windows VM. Ids are followed by a comment with their friendly name.

install.description: Packages to install: winget ids (they contain a dot), Microsoft Store ids, or aliases from HyperHarbor's package catalog (resolved when the profile is applied).

appx.description: Provisioned Appx package names without the version, for example Microsoft.BingNews.

capabilities.description: Windows capability names, for example Browser.InternetExplorer~~~~0.0.11.0.

features.description: Optional feature names, for example MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root.

programs.description: Host profiles only: ids from the host's program catalog (catalogs/host-programs.yaml), for example onedrive.

app.description: The browser's winget id or alias: Google.Chrome, Microsoft.Edge, or Brave.Brave.

extensions.description: Chrome Web Store ids (32 letters a to p), or edge:<id> for the Edge Add-ons store.

policies.description: Browser policies by friendly key, from HyperHarbor's browser catalog.

target.description: Where the profile applies. Without a target it is a VM profile; host profiles belong to the Lean host action.

services.description: Host profiles only: service names with their startup type.

startup.description: Host profiles only: startup entries (Run keys and Startup folders) by name, with * and ? wildcards. Disabling writes StartupApproved and removes nothing. The built-in allowlist and keep are never disabled.

power.description: Host profiles only: the power plan and which devices may wake the PC.

plan.description: highPerformance, ultimate, balanced, powerSaver, or a plan GUID.

wake.description: nicOnly lets only network adapters wake the PC; nicAndInput also keeps keyboards and mice that may wake it now.

armWake.description: Device names, as powercfg lists them, that may wake the PC.

value.description: Not needed for absent, which deletes the value.
